column6: Bullet 1 stated Perec's motive as 'because' e is most common and called the constraint 'as hard as it can be'; motive was also thematic/autobiographical. Reworded to a plain fact: e is the hardest single letter to omit in French.
Older text (not fixed): q0 and q1 question strings end with a stray double quote; Explainer cites English words 'there'/'three' as examples for a French novel.
Checked 3x3x3x3 = 81 for three swappable four-line stanzas.
Exquisite corpse is a Surrealist game derived from the parlor game 'consequences'; 'parlor games such as' left as acceptable.

Bullet 1 is correct (Jackson's creature is the unfinished female companion). Older text (not fixed) contradicts it: Explainer para 1 and q1 explanation say Jackson 'recasts the creature as female'; q1 option 0 calls the original monster 'female-coded'.
Style only: banned word 'essential' replaced with 'fixed in an essence'.
Bullet 1 correction was absolute (audiobooks always perform page texts; podcasts always written for audio); audio-original audiobooks and adapted podcasts exist. Added 'usually'/'Most'.
Older text: Core Idea uses banned word 'fosters' (not in scope, not fixed).

Older text (not fixed): q4 explanation and Explainer say Twine variables are 'implemented visually, not through typed code' (they are typed macros/markup); Explainer dates Twine to 'early 2010s' (released 2009, popularized c. 2012-14).
Bullet 1 copied the Explainer's overstatement 'flash fiction works at longer lengths'; micro forms of flash fiction can be tweet-length. Added 'usually runs to hundreds of words'.
Checked Herbert 'Easter Wings' as a shaped poem (1633).
Checked Colossal Cave Adventure predates and inspired Zork.
